Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. It has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal and an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line. AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

Your stated objective is to have governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. The Client's regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. Customer data must stay in the EU, and the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff. ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year, with the start date not yet fixed.

**What the Briefing covers for the Client**

The Briefing is designed for an audience of General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. It covers four areas.

First, it reviews EU AI Act and GDPR expectations that may apply to each use case. These include transparency for the chatbot, whether the visual inspection system falls within a high-risk category and EU data residency. All of these are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States expectations appear only as a general landscape item.

Second, it holds a readiness discussion at the Client's piloting maturity level, using the Q2 2027 objective as the reference point.

Third, it gives an overview of a governance operating model drawn from the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Board-level oversight is referenced to AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). The model is anchored in Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

Fourth, it sets out implementation priorities and decision points, including how governance work could prepare for ISO/IEC 42001. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Logistics and price**

The Executive Briefing runs for two hours, live virtual, at US$3,000.

**What the Client receives afterward**

The Client receives a post-briefing summary memo. It records the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option.

**Next step**

The decision timeline is not yet known. We propose a short intake call to confirm a date and three questions:

1. Does the visual inspection pilot fall within the works council consultation commitment?
2. Which governance frameworks does the Client already use?
3. Should any AI risk events inform the discussion?

Yours sincerely,

AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
